scores.notes: Alice beside the mushroom and facing the bench shares long golden-brown hair, fair skin, a small youthful face and a slim childlike build. Her size relative to the surroundings does not change those cues.

The floating head and the cat on the branch share grey-brown tabby stripes, pale muzzle, pink nose, greenish eyes and a broad toothy grin; the absence of a body on the left does not alter the recognizable head.

Alice drinking and Alice in the armchair both have fair skin, long golden-brown hair, a small pointed chin and similar youthful facial features; the flying hair and frown account for the pose difference.
The seated and drinking Alice shares long wavy golden-brown hair, rosy fair cheeks, a small nose and the same young child's facial proportions.
Alice at the tea table and beside the mushroom shares golden-brown hair past her shoulders, fair rosy skin, a small pointed chin and similar young facial proportions.

Both views show a grassy croquet ground with conspicuous parallel furrows, card-patterned hoops, clipped hedges and tall trees beyond the garden boundary. The different angles are compatible with the same enclosed garden.
The tea-table Hatter has grey wispy hair at the temples and a deeply lined, older face; the courtroom Hatter has thick dark brown curls and a smoother, younger-looking face.

Both show a long tea table beneath a massive spreading tree, with an ivy-covered gabled brick cottage and leaded windows behind it. The closer left viewpoint and shade are compatible with that same garden.
The courtroom Hatter has long straw-brown wisps and a narrow drooping face with a small chin; the tea-table Hatter has shorter dark-grey hair, a heavier angular jaw and more deeply aged features.

Alice holding the flamingo and standing by the mushroom shares long wavy golden-brown hair, fair skin, a small nose and a youthful oval face. The change in apron and posture does not conflict with those identity cues.

Both show a white-clothed tea table under a huge spreading tree next to an ivy-covered gabled cottage with diamond-paned windows. The cottage's position changes compatibly with viewing the table from another side.

Alice with the flamingo and before the bench shares long golden-brown hair, a dark hairband, fair skin, small nose and youthful profile; her smaller scale in the courtroom does not establish a different identity.

Behind the tree, the left has an irregular ivy-covered brick cottage with steep front gables and diamond-paned windows; the right has a plain symmetrical pale house with a hipped roof, sash windows and a classical triangular door pediment.
Alice drinking and Alice beside the Caterpillar has the same long golden-brown wavy hair, fair skin, small nose and youthful oval face; the different sleeves and apron are clothing changes.

Both Alices have fair rosy skin, golden-brown hair extending below the shoulders, a small pointed chin and similar youthful features. The windblown hair and larger depiction on the right do not alone change identity.

The left background house is a tall, narrow building with horizontal wooden siding and projecting bay windows; the right cottage has pale masonry, exposed timber in the gable and broad diamond-paned windows. Those building materials and facade forms conflict.
Alice with the flamingo and in the armchair shares golden-brown shoulder-length waves, a dark hairband, fair skin and the same youthful oval face.

The courtroom and tea-table Alice has matching golden-brown hair and hairband, fair skin, small nose and youthful facial proportions; the side view and greater distance in the courtroom remain recognizable.

The left ground is enclosed by very tall solid hedges with a high arched iron gate and irregular bare patches; the right has low clipped hedges below exposed pale garden walls, rose borders and regular parallel furrows.
Alice in court and holding the flamingo shares long wavy golden-brown hair, a dark hairband, fair rosy skin, a small nose and a similar young face despite her different pose and scale.

The left has a broad worn, rutted playing area enclosed by towering hedges and an arched iron gate. The right has a much more even grassy lawn with low rose-lined garden walls and separated clipped shrubs, conflicting in ground and boundary layout.

The flamingo-holder and bottle-drinker share golden-brown hair below the shoulders, fair rosy skin, a small nose and pointed chin. The hair blowing outward on the right changes its pose rather than its recognizable color and length.

The courtroom Alice and the girl beside the mushroom share long wavy golden-brown hair, fair skin, small youthful oval faces and similar slim builds; the clothing differences do not establish another person.

Both show a sunlit grassy croquet ground with ridged furrows, patterned hoops and clipped hedges backed by tall trees. The exposed wall in part of the left view is compatible with the hedge-screened boundary at right.

Alice beside the mushroom and holding the flamingo shares long golden-brown hair, fair rosy skin, a small nose and pointed youthful chin. The hairband and slight wave difference do not outweigh the matching face.
The bottle-drinking Alice and flamingo-holder have matching long golden-brown waves, fair rosy skin, small nose and young oval face, despite leaning in different directions.

The left background has an ivy-covered cottage with steep projecting gables and small leaded windows; the right shows a broad plain symmetrical house with a hipped roof, sash windows and a triangular door pediment.
Alice in the armchair and with the flamingo shares long golden-brown wavy hair, fair rosy cheeks, a small nose and similar young facial proportions.

The left background building has horizontal wooden siding, tall projecting bays and narrow gables; the right has a broad ivy-clad brick facade with large diamond-paned windows. The differing facade construction is not explained by the table viewpoint.
The bottle-drinking and courtroom Alice has matching long golden-brown wavy hair, fair skin, small nose and young oval face; her scale within each room differs without a clear identity conflict.
Both show the same kind of furrowed grassy croquet lawn, patterned hoops, clipped hedges, pale boundary wall and tall trees. Their arrangement is compatible with nearby viewpoints in one garden.

The left lawn has deep parallel earth furrows running across almost the entire playing surface; the right playing area is a relatively level continuous grassy lawn. The similar walls and shrubs do not explain that substantial ground change at the same occasion.

Alice beside the Caterpillar and in the armchair shares long wavy golden-brown hair, fair skin, a small nose and similar young facial proportions; her dress and apron differ but her identity cues remain.
The seated tea-party Alice and standing courtroom Alice has matching long golden-brown waves, fair rosy cheeks, a small chin and a youthful oval face.

The branch cat and floating head have matching grey-brown tabby stripes, pale muzzle, pink nose, pointed ears and a broad toothy grin. The eyes are opened more widely on the left, consistent with expression.

Alice in court and drinking from the bottle shares golden-brown hair below the shoulders, fair rosy skin, a small nose and pointed youthful chin. The different scale and flowing hair do not provide a conflicting identity cue.
